meta.name: decision_continuity
meta.purpose: Synthetic multi-session scenarios for the cross-session decision continuity contract: establish a decision, later correct/challenge it, restart, then perform a task that depends on it. Every scenario is driven through the real kumiho_memory MCP tool handlers over an in-memory SDK fake; no LLM key, no network.
meta.split_rule: `dev` scenarios were authored while the harness was written and may have shaped it. `heldout` scenarios were authored afterwards, with different subject matter, and were not looked at while implementing checks; they are frozen with this file and must not be edited to make a candidate pass. New held-out cases go into a new fixture version.
meta.scoring_rule: Outcomes are structured labels read from `option:*` tags (or the scenario's declared per-language `option_signals`), never free-text keyword matching. A scenario passes when every named check passes; checks are deterministic assertions on the tool results and the graph state. Item counts and trial counts are reported separately; this tier runs one trial per scenario because it is deterministic.

boundaries.new_host_session: a new session id, a fresh working-memory (Redis) instance and a fresh manager process; only the long-term graph is shared in the memory arm
boundaries.process_restart: the same session id and working memory, but a fresh manager process (module singleton reset, recall dedup cache cleared)

arms.B: memory: sessions share one long-term graph
arms.A: no memory: every session gets an empty graph and an empty working memory; the final task sees nothing
arms.Bprime: decoy: agent tier only (a generic authoritative brief cannot change a scripted agent); `decoy_brief` is carried for that tier and is not executed here

meta.option_signals_note: typed facts carry no tags; scenarios that read typed facts declare `option_signals` per language so the structured outcome is still a declared mapping, not English keyword matching
